name: Silk Hour
summary: A live clock told by a brass spider on a rippling web, with legs for hands
about: A working clock drawn as a spider web under a moon. A little brass spider hangs from a silk thread: its two long legs are the hour and minute hands, a dewdrop with a fading trail runs round the rim for the seconds, and the web ripples whenever it is touched. Good for a watch shop, a Halloween page or a quirky portfolio.
how: The clock reads your device time; the spider sways on its silk and its eyes follow your pointer.
Brush the web with your pointer and ripples travel along the threads.
Tap the spider (or focus it and press Enter): it bounces and swings, its legs flail, dewdrops fall and a bubble tells you the time.
Each new minute the minute leg taps the web, and on the hour the whole web chimes with a ring of light.
Switch 12/24-hour or smooth/ticking seconds; with reduced motion the web stays still and the seconds tick.
